current_text.html: Witnesses shall be examined first by the party introducing them; then cross-examined by the opposite party; after which any member of the court, or either party, may put additional interrogatories. No question shall be put or answered except by permission of the moderator, subject to an appeal to the court. The court shall not permit questions frivolous or irrelevant to the charge at issue.

metadata.synopsis: A filing challenging Presbytery’s handling of Huffman’s BCO 38-1 confession was styled as an appeal under a newly amended rule. The SJC found it judicially out of order because the case began and was nearly completed when the former rule provided review by complaint, and retroactive application would be unfair. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the filing as a complaint at its next stated meeting; denial or failure to act permits review by the SJC. No merits issue was decided.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.

relationships.title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley

metadata.synopsis: A claimant sought BCO 40-5 review of Presbytery’s handling of his earlier judicial case, alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings and delinquency in failing to investigate his 2012 deposition. The SJC found the application administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 40-3 excludes judicial-case proceedings from review and control when notice of appeal or complaint has been given, and he had withdrawn his 2012 complaint acknowledging it could not be resubmitted. It dismissed under OMSJC 9.2(d). The concurrence added that BCO 40 cannot refile a withdrawn complaint or reverse a censure.

metadata.synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his Metro Atlanta Presbytery conviction on three charges of breaking ordination vows and indefinite suspension, alleging seventeen procedural and evidentiary errors. Applying BCO 39-2/3 clear-error deference, the SJC denied every specification and upheld the judgment and censure. It found no clear error in the BCO 31-2 investigation, indictment/prosecutor process, commission membership, evidence rulings, scheduling, alleged prejudice, or censure. It assessed transcription costs equally while encouraging MAP to absorb them, and cautioned that an absent commissioner's vote might support a future challenge.

A presbytery deposed a minister for violating his seventh vow by pursuing an unbiblical divorce after he filed a civil petition. The SJC sustained the appeal in part: the presbytery clearly erred in finding sin in the filing, because the record did not conclusively show intent to divorce rather than protect his children, and the wife's counter-filing undermined the failure-to-withdraw inference. The SJC rejected prejudice, irregularity, and venue claims, voided the trial judgment, and noted that his expired prior suspension left him a presbytery member without call. Divorce precedents are fact-specific.

metadata.synopsis: G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery, which failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case, causing irremediable injury. The SJC did not reach the merits; it suspended the lower judgment indefinitely, dismissed the appeal under BCO 42-7, rebuked Pacific Presbytery, and urged greater care in preserving, transcribing, and transmitting testimony. Dismissal therefore did not leave the challenged judgment enforceable. A separate concurrence suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter and questioned imprudent prosecutions.

occurrences.excerpt: The seventh specification of error alleges that the JC violated BCO 35-7 by allowing testimony to be erased from the recording of the trial before it was transcribed. This specification is not sustained. There is no evidence that this erasure was deliberate…

metadata.synopsis: A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another.

metadata.synopsis: Joined with Case 2009-25; the Session of Grace Presbyterian Church complained that views 3, 4, 5, and 6 in Northern California Presbytery's resolution on diaconal practice violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint on the same grounds as 2009-25, annulling the abstract resolution while declining to rule on the constitutional merits of any specific diaconal view.

Nashville Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of reports against TE George Grant was inadequately documented and internally inconsistent, and the evidence before Presbytery raised a strong presumption of guilt, the SJC held. It sustained the complaint, ruling that pastoral reconciliation does not displace the duty to institute judicial process, and remanded for further proceedings; it did not adjudicate Grant guilty. A concurrence agreed only in remanding to supplement the record under BCO 42-5 & 7.

metadata.synopsis: A complaint challenged Siouxlands Presbytery's investigation of allegations that TE Joshua Moon held heterodox Federal Vision views and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC held that Presbytery had investigated diligently under BCO 31-2 and, deferring under BCO 39-3 to its credibility judgment, found no clear error. It declined to decide whether the overture should have been treated as charges because that issue was not raised below, while leaving future charges possible. A concurrence favored charges; the dissent would have found error and remanded.

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. The SJC sustained the appeal: unauthorized committee citations and admonition without process could not support guilt, and multiple trial violations were fatally prejudicial. It set aside the judgment, dismissed the citation and admonition charges, and revoked both censures. The inappropriate-language charge was not adjudicated on its merits; Presbytery could retry it on remand or dismiss it.

metadata.synopsis: Case 2002-18 is a complaint (the heading also says "Reference") identified in the adopted motion as TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery. The SJC found it judicially out of order because it was filed against actions of a judicial commission, not completed Presbytery actions (BCO 15-3, 43-1). The full SJC approved that action on October 16, 2003. No merits ruling or later dismissal is stated; the Manual only outlines a possible dismissal route.

metadata.synopsis: Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. Chavalas’s later resignation did not abandon the appeal because he had appealed beforehand after a regular trial; no rebuke was issued.
